newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ends lower as tech stocks weakened.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ends lower as tech stocks weakened.

text.p: Nasdaq started the year with a thud as technology stocks weakened and stronger-than-expected manufacturing data rattled the market.

The Nasdaq Composite Index ended down 10.33 or 0.80 percent at 1280.70 after recovering from a midday low of 1272.52. The Dow rallied from earlier losses and unofficially closed down 6 at 6442. The long bond sank 1-7/32 to yield 6.74 percent after a report showed manufacturing activity remained healthy in December.

"The bond market was the big culprit of the day. CompUSA helped the techs slid, but the big factor was the bonds" said Barry Berman, head of equity trading at Robert W. Baird and Co. "Stocks were down all day, but there was a strong rally late in the day as some buy programs kicked in," he said.
Some technology stocks softened after computer retailer CompUSA Inc posted a disappointing 1.5 percent gain in December same-store sales.
Dell Computer Corp dropped 1-7/8 to 51-1/4. Intel Corp pared midday losses and closed down just 9/16 to 130-3/8. Microsoft Corp shed 1 to 81-5/8.
Losing stocks beat gaining stocks 2414 to 1955 on total volume of 502 million shares.
